charge_sentences: title: >- Charge the decomposition oracle's MEMORY, symmetrically with the rho

objective: >- Settle, for the whole decomposition-oracle family rather than one oracle, whether ANY summand count can put index calculus below rho on a binary curve once the oracle's memory is charged on the same footing as the baseline's.

A meet-in-the-middle decomposition oracle is exactly the kind of algorithm whose apparent advantage lives in its store, so charging one side and not the other is the single largest unexamined asymmetry in this program's comparison.
The product law is independent of dim V, so with the oracle charged NOTHING the m = 3 floor is already 2^68.58 against rho's 2^60.8090 (EV-ICPERF-10c5fc, KN-FIND-aa2efc).
meaningful: the index-calculus side's store buys TIME, the baseline's does not, so charging memory cannot disadvantage rho unfairly.
id: C-NULL-NO-MEMORY-CHARGE
Re-run the whole sweep with the store charged at zero, so MITM_CAPPED collapses to MITM at every B.
If the sub-rho cells are the same with and without the memory charge, the charge is buying nothing and the result is about the product law alone, not about memory.
pass_criterion: >- diagnostic, reported either way; a null that matches the charged sweep REFUTES this contract's premise and must be reported as such -
supersedes: controls[C-NULL-NO-MEMORY-CHARGE]
Re-running with the store charged at zero collapses MITM_CAPPED to MITM, whose feasible cells are a strict SUPERSET of the capped ones whenever B binds.
finding: >- "CHARGE THE ORACLE'S MEMORY" OVERSTATES WHAT IS COMPUTED.
The oracle's store is BUDGET-CONSTRAINED (s <= floor(log2 B / d)) and reported; rho's work is invariant along its own curve and its memory is reported, not charged.
No record derived from this experiment -- no EV-*, no DEC-*, and above all no KN-FIND title -- may state that memory was charged into a cost.

degree_or_curve_sentences: statement: >- On a binary curve of prime extension degree n, an m-summand index calculus whose decomposition oracle is a generic m-SUM search cannot fall below the van Oorschot-Wiener rho baseline at any summand count without a store whose size exceeds rho's entire work.

predictions: - >- Memory-free enumeration gives a total independent of d and of m, so no factor-base tuning and no summand count rescues it. - >- With store free, the first summand count strictly below the published ECC2K-130 reference is m = 8. - >- The minimum store admitting any sub-rho cell has exponent at least n/2 at every m, minimised near m = 8. - >- No store budget at or below 2^80 admits a sub-rho cell at any binary degree the program tracks.
The curve's group structure -- Frobenius, the 2-torsion, the low-degree function field -- is where such an algorithm would come from, and none of those has produced one here.
random_model_justification: >- Inherited from H-SEMBIN-97ea23 (status: supported), where it is stated and justified.

The statement is about concrete store exponents at named degrees, not about an exponent in n, and dressing it as asymptotic would invite the promotion gates of docs/target-result-profile.md Part D for a claim it does not make.
RQ-SEMBIN-9fa4ba is GOAL-SEMBIN-cbf422's question and its four objects are chain length t = m, path chaining topology, low-degree subspace V, and the absorbed n^{4 omega} cofactor.

The memory-charged cost lane is GOAL-SEMBIN-5078bc's: its objective item (4) COST asks for time AND memory against a rho comparator with negligible memory (KN-OPEN-86e7e1), its completion criterion 4 asks for exactly a time-and-memory record against vOW parallel rho with a tradeoff curve in m, H-SEMBIN-97ea23 -- the supported baseline-coherence result this hypothesis builds on -- is that goal's, and GOAL-SEMBIN-cbf422's own committed identifier note states that "the memory-charged crossover work is EXP-SEMBIN-f4a17b under GOAL-SEMBIN-5078bc".

The memory-charged cost lane is GOAL-SEMBIN-5078bc's: its objective item (4) COST asks for time AND memory against a rho comparator with negligible memory (KN-OPEN-86e7e1), its completion criterion 4 asks for exactly a time-and-memory record against vOW parallel rho with a tradeoff curve in m, H-SEMBIN-97ea23 -- the supported baseline-coherence result this hypothesis builds on -- is that goal's, and GOAL-SEMBIN-cbf422's own committed identifier note states that "the memory-charged crossover work is EXP-SEMBIN-f4a17b under GOAL-SEMBIN-5078bc".

No record in this program bounds the decomposition-oracle family by memory at any summand count; the committed free-oracle floor charges the oracle nothing at all, and the measured panel is m = 3 only.

degree_or_curve_sentences: To put an m-summand index calculus below the rho baseline on a binary curve, with the decomposition oracle's store charged on the same footing as the baseline's, the store must exceed rho's ENTIRE WORK at every degree tested -- by 37.1 bits at n=97 rising to 90.6 bits at n=571.
On ECC2K-130 the cheapest entry costs 2^106.8 of store to reach a 2^64.2 attack, against a baseline whose total work is 2^64.3.
The minimising summand count drifts 8, 8, 8, 8, 10, 10, 10, 10, 12, 14 across the ten degrees.
Those 14 survivors sit only at n=97 and n=109, need 2^90 of store or more, and both those curves were solved by rho in 1998 and 1999.
No cell at a store budget of 2^80 or below falls below either baseline at any degree.
Independent review is owed and is TASK-20260928-e4f7b2.
